name: South of England: London, Bath, Oxford and Brighton

cities.base: Southwark and Bankside: Borough Market, Tate Modern and the Globe on foot, London Bridge for Brighton trains, one stop to the City and two to the West End.
cities.name: London

cities.base: The Georgian streets between Queen Square and the Circus: the Baths, the Abbey, the Crescent, the Raven and the Beckford places all on foot, above the tour-group crush.
cities.name: Bath

cities.base: Inside the old centre, round the High Street and Radcliffe Square: the colleges, the Ashmolean, the Covered Market and the Turf are all a short walk.
cities.name: Oxford

cities.base: The Lanes: English's, the Cricketers and a dozen dinners on the doorstep, the Royal Pavilion five minutes one way and the Palace Pier five the other.
cities.name: Brighton

cities.base: Nobody needs a night here; direct trains from Paddington (via Slough) or Waterloo take 40 to 55 minutes.
cities.name: Windsor

cities.base: No train reaches these villages: a car or a tour coach from Oxford or Bath, and Bourton and Bibury fit in one day.
cities.name: Cotswolds villages

places.name: British Museum
places.note: Free permanent collection, 10:00 to 17:00 and to 20:30 on Fridays, last entry 30 to 45 minutes before close, shut 24 to 26 December. The Rosetta Stone and Parthenon sculptures queue at opening, so take the Friday evening; special exhibitions are ticketed.

places.name: Tower of London
places.note: Adults £37 to 30 September 2026, £38 from 1 October; it opens 10:00 on Mondays and 11:00 on Sundays, last entry 16:30. Walk straight to a Yeoman Warder tour at opening (the last goes at 15:15); some rooms shut in rotation for conservation.

places.name: Tate Modern
places.note: Free permanent collection every day, open to 21:00 on Friday and Saturday, last entry 30 minutes before close. Check this year's Turbine Hall piece, then ride up to the Level 10 terrace for a free 360-degree view of St Paul's and the City.

places.name: Borough Market
places.note: Over 100 traders; shut Mondays, Saturday from 09:00, Sunday to 16:00. Come for lunch, not dinner, since most stalls are done by 17:00, and get into the grilled cheese and salt beef queues before noon.

places.name: Padella
places.note: No bookings: scan the QR code on arrival to join the virtual queue, and Sundays end at 21:00. Order the pici cacio e pepe (£13.50) and the 8-hour beef shin pappardelle (£16.50); the pasta is rolled by hand in the front window.

places.name: St. JOHN Smithfield
places.note: The nose-to-tail kitchen that reset British cooking in the 1990s, still chef-owned. Order the bone marrow and parsley salad, on the menu since day one; the menu is posted each morning, book for dinner, and Sunday is lunch alone, done by 16:00.

places.name: Dishoom Shoreditch
places.note: Bombay-café breakfast from 08:00 (09:00 at weekends), open to midnight Thursday to Saturday. Bacon naan roll in the morning, prawn pathia and house black daal at night; bookings are for 6 or more after 18:00, so a pair just walks in.

places.name: Beigel Bake
places.note: Open 24 hours, every day, since 1979. Order the salt beef beigel with mustard and a pickle at the counter and eat it walking up Brick Lane; there is nearly always a queue, it moves fast, and card or cash both work.

places.name: E Pellicci
places.note: Family-run since 1900, with Grade II-listed Art Deco marquetry inside, and billed as London's oldest family café. Order the full English or the bubble and squeak; cash moves faster than card, and it is shut on Sundays.

places.name: Trullo
places.note: Handmade pasta and charcoal-grilled meat and fish in Highbury since 2010, praised by Jay Rayner in the Observer. Order whichever pasta is on the day's menu, eat at the bar if the tables are full, and allow 20 minutes by bus or Overground; 21:30 on Sundays.

places.name: Columbia Road Flower Market
places.note: The flower stalls trade on Sundays, roughly 08:00 to 15:00, while the 60 shops on the street open other days too. Be there by 09:00 for room to move and the sellers' patter at full volume; by 14:00 they cut prices to clear stock.

places.name: Shakespeare's Globe
places.note: The rebuilt 1599 open-air theatre, 200m from the original site; the guided tour takes in the exhibition and runs 25 September 2026 to 31 January 2027. Hours vary, check, and check the price, which was not listed.

places.name: St Paul's Cathedral
places.note: Wren's cathedral, with the climb to the Whispering Gallery and on up the dome; guided and self-guided tours run every day. Hours vary, check, and check the price, which was not confirmed.

places.name: Portobello Road Market
places.note: Nearly a mile of stalls: antiques near Notting Hill Gate, fruit and veg further north, vintage and street food under the Westway. Saturday is the antiques day; come before 10:00 for the dealers and at midday to eat. Trading days unconfirmed, check.

places.name: Kensington Gardens
places.note: Pedestrian gates open 06:00 to 19:30. The Peter Pan statue by the Long Water and the Italian Gardens are the two stops worth the detour, and Kensington Palace on the west edge adds a ticketed indoor stop.

places.name: Sky Garden
places.note: A free viewing deck at the top of the Walkie-Talkie tower, but you need a timed slot booked online, and the sunset slots go first; book a week ahead. Hours vary, check.

places.name: The Anchor Bankside
places.note: Rebuilt in 1676 after the Great Fire, on the Thames path between the Globe and Borough Market; Saturday opens 10:00, and it runs to 23:30 Thursday to Saturday. The beer garden takes no bookings, so arrive before 18:00 on a warm evening; food to 22:00.

places.name: The Grapes
places.note: Five centuries on the river, written into Dickens' Our Mutual Friend and part-owned by Ian McKellen; the heated deck hangs over the water. No table bookings, no under-18s, 22:30 on Sundays, and 20 minutes' walk or a DLR ride east of the City.

places.name: Roman Baths
places.note: The 2,000-year-old Roman bathing complex round the original spring, audio guide with most tickets. Autumn 2026 hours are 09:00 to 18:00, last entry 17:00, and change by season. Book a timed slot, weekends sell out, and check the price, which was not listed.

places.name: Bath Abbey
places.note: £9 adults, audio guide £3.50 more, last entry 30 minutes before close; the fan vaulting was finished in the 1860s. Saturday runs to 18:00, but Sunday opening is just 13:00 to 15:30 round services, so do not plan a Sunday morning here.

places.name: Sally Lunn's
places.note: In what is billed as Bath's oldest house (1480s), with the original bakery kitchen shown as a small museum downstairs. Order the Sally Lunn bun, sweet or savoury topping; it is priced for tourists, so come for the bun, not a full dinner.

places.name: The Scallop Shell
places.note: The fish and chips locals rate: cod or haddock in a light batter, chips cut fresh each day. On Sundays it shuts at 15:00 with no evening service, so make that a lunch.

places.name: Thermae Bath Spa
places.note: The one natural thermal spa in the UK you can bathe in; the open-air rooftop pool looks over the Abbey and the hills. The 2-hour Welcome session is £44 on weekdays and £49 at weekends; book online, as walk-ins get turned away at weekends. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Royal Crescent
places.note: 30 Grade I-listed Georgian houses in one sweep, finished in 1774, free to walk and photograph from the lawn. No.1 at the end is a paid house-museum whose hours were not confirmed, so check before counting on it.

places.name: Pulteney Bridge
places.note: One of a handful of bridges in the world lined with shops on both sides, Florence's Ponte Vecchio being the famous other. The photograph is from below it: the Parade Gardens side, or a boat trip on the Pulteney Weir.

places.name: Bath Skyline walk
places.note: A 6-mile National Trust waymarked loop through fields and woods above the city, with views back over the Georgian skyline. Quiet in a way the centre never is; start in the morning and wear boots after rain.

places.name: The Raven of Bath
places.note: A no-fuss two-bar pub by Queen Square with pies, sausage and mash, and a rotating line of real ales and ciders. No bookings; it is where locals send you, open to midnight Friday and Saturday and 22:30 on Sunday.

places.name: Beckford Bottle Shop
places.note: Wine merchant and bistro with over thirty wines by the glass and Bib Gourmand-listed small plates, cheese and charcuterie. Come for a glass before dinner rather than the whole meal; closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Landrace Bakery
places.note: Sourdough bakery and café from 08:30 to 15:30, walk-ins, that turns into a small booked dinner room and a walk-in pizzeria at night. Come for the morning pastries, or book the upstairs dinner.

places.name: The Marlborough Tavern
places.note: A 200-year-old gastropub two streets behind the Royal Crescent, with two AA rosettes and a seasonal local menu. Book for dinner, there is no parking, and hours vary, check.

places.name: The Chequers
places.note: Bib Gourmand gastropub on a quiet Georgian street; order the Orkney scallops or the Wiltshire pheasant, or a blackboard special. Weekdays it opens at 15:00, weekends at noon, and Sunday ends at 19:30.

places.name: Beckford Canteen
places.note: Sister to the Beckford Bottle Shop, listed by Michelin for seasonal British small plates. Closed Monday and Tuesday, and Sunday runs 12:00 to 18:00; book for dinner, lunch is easier to walk into.

places.name: Jane Austen Centre
places.note: Not her house but a costumed exhibition on her five years in Bath, on the street where she once lodged. Adults £17, last entry an hour before close, and the hours shrink in autumn and winter, so check the seasonal calendar.

places.name: American Museum & Gardens
places.note: The one museum of American decorative arts outside the US, in a Georgian manor over the Avon valley: quilts, folk art, Native American galleries, period rooms, and gardens worth autumn. Closed Mondays outside holidays, shut early January to mid-February; no rail.

places.name: Holburne Museum
places.note: Free permanent collection of paintings, silver and porcelain in a converted hotel at the end of Great Pulteney Street, with a garden café behind. Sundays open 11:00, last entry 16:30; five minutes' walk past Sydney Gardens from Pulteney Bridge.

places.name: The Circus
places.note: John Wood the Elder's ring of thirty townhouses (1754 to 1768), the pair to the Royal Crescent a short walk away. Free, no ticket; look from under the plane trees on the centre lawn rather than from the road.
places.neighborhood: Between the Royal Crescent and Gay Street

places.name: Bodleian Library
places.note: Main buildings from 1602; the Divinity School played the Hogwarts infirmary. Tours come in mini, standard and extended tiers at different prices, so book the one you want online first. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Ashmolean Museum
places.note: Free, daily 10:00 to 17:00, last entry 16:45; Britain's oldest public museum (1683). Do not skip the Ashurbanipal reliefs or the Alfred Jewel, and the rooftop restaurant is lunch with a view over the skyline.

places.name: Christ Church College & Cathedral
places.note: Wren's Tom Tower, a cathedral that is also the college chapel, and the hall behind Harry Potter's Great Hall; Lewis Carroll taught maths here. It shuts to visitors for exams and evensong, so hours vary, check the calendar, and check the price.

places.name: Oxford Covered Market
places.note: Roofed market trading since 1774: butchers, cheesemongers, a barber and several cafés, not a tourist food hall. A daytime place that shuts in the evening; hours vary, check.
places.neighborhood: Between High Street and Market Street

places.name: The Trout Inn
places.note: Riverside pub with a terrace over the Thames weir, on the Inspector Morse trail and once a haunt of C.S. Lewis's circle. A 30 to 40 minute walk or short taxi north, off the main bus routes; 22:30 on Sundays.

places.name: The Turf Tavern
places.note: Grade II-listed, from 1381, down two narrow passages that first-timers walk past; C.S. Lewis and Richard Burton drank here. 12 real ales, food to 21:00, and no bookings from May to September.

places.name: The King's Arms
places.note: Pouring since 1607 and claims to be Oxford's oldest pub, with cask ales and a proper Sunday roast. Sunday opens 11:00; food stops at 22:00 (21:00 Sunday) but the bar runs to midnight, so it is the late pint after dinner.

places.name: The Vaults and Garden
places.note: A café in the medieval Old Congregation House by the University Church, with tables in the walled garden. Order the cream tea or the curry-and-salad lunch; it is a daytime place, done by 17:00 (17:30 Saturday), no dinner.

places.name: Arbequina
places.note: Spanish tapas and natural wine praised by the Guardian and the New York Times; order the tortilla and share plates at the zinc bar. Open Thursday to Saturday, dinner apart from a Saturday lunch, with a 14:45 to 16:30 break that afternoon.

places.name: No.1 Ship Street
places.note: Modern British brasserie that has won Time Out's Oxfordshire best-restaurant award several years running; the splurge night, a step up from a pub dinner. Hours vary, check, and book.

places.name: Edamame
places.note: A tiny Japanese home-cooking room with rotating lunch, sushi-night and dinner menus, cash preferred and no bookings, so expect a queue on the pavement. Closed Monday and Tuesday; Wednesday is lunch alone and Sunday ends at 15:30.

places.name: Pitt Rivers Museum
places.note: Free anthropology and archaeology packed floor to ceiling; the shrunken heads case is the one everyone remembers. Enter through the Natural History Museum on Parks Road, and on Mondays it opens at 12:00.
places.neighborhood: Entered via the Natural History Museum

places.name: Oxford University Museum of Natural History
places.note: Free; the world's first purpose-built natural history museum (1860), a glass-and-iron hall of dinosaur skeletons with the Pitt Rivers through the back. Last entry 16:45; a critical-minerals exhibition runs to April 2027.

places.name: University Church of St Mary the Virgin
places.note: The university church since medieval times and the cheapest tower climb in the city, looking down on the Radcliffe Camera and the colleges. Sundays run 12:00 to 18:00 round services.

places.name: Radcliffe Camera
places.note: Gibbs' 1749 round Bodleian reading room, the most photographed building in Oxford. You cannot walk in except on a booked Bodleian tour, so treat it as a 20 minute stop outside, free from the square.

places.name: Magdalen College
places.note: The richest college and by most students' vote the prettiest, with a deer park, a riverside walk and the 144-foot tower where choristers sing at dawn on 1 May. Hours vary, check, and check the price, which was not confirmed.

places.name: Oxford Castle & Prison
places.note: A Norman motte-and-bailey turned Victorian prison: climb St George's Tower and walk the old cells on an actor-led tour. Open all year; the price was not confirmed, roughly £15 to £20, so check before booking.

places.name: University Parks
places.note: 70 acres of lawns and the Cherwell along Mesopotamia Walk, free, from 07:45 to dusk every day but Christmas Eve; hire a punt at the Cherwell Boathouse at the north end. The quiet answer to a morning of colleges.

places.name: Brighton Palace Pier
places.note: Free to walk, with rides and arcade games paid per go; fish and chips and doughnuts at the entrance are the classic order. 10:00 to 21:00 when checked, but the closing time moves with the season.

places.name: Royal Pavilion
places.note: George IV's Indo-Saracenic seaside palace; the Music Room and its gilded dome are the reason to go. £21.50, 90 minutes. October to March 10:00 to 17:15, April to September 09:30 to 17:45, last in 16:30 in winter; shut all day 18 November 2026, Saturday tour at 14:00.

places.name: The Lanes
places.note: The tangle of old fishing-town lanes, now antique jewellers, boutiques and cafés keeping daytime hours; packed at weekends. Not the same place as the North Laine further north, and locals will correct you.
places.neighborhood: Between North Street and the seafront

places.name: British Airways i360
places.note: A glass pod up a 162m tower, reopened in March 2025 under new owners and trading in 2026. Roughly 10:30 to 19:00 into October, 11:00 to 16:00 in November and December, shut 4 to 28 January, and it stops in high wind. Check the price.

places.name: English's of Brighton
places.note: Family-run since 1945 and billed as the city's oldest seafood restaurant and oyster bar, with old-school silver service; start with the oysters. Hours vary, check.

places.name: The Chilli Pickle
places.note: Regional Indian street food and kebabs, not a curry-house menu; order the barbecue surf and turf. Closed Tuesdays; other weekdays break 15:00 to 17:00, Saturday runs straight through, Sunday ends at 20:30.

places.name: The Cricketers
places.note: Brighton's oldest pub, a Lanes fixture with live music and darts. The kitchen stops at 20:00 or 21:00 depending on the day, and the bar runs to 02:00 on Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Terre à Terre
places.note: Vegetarian and vegan since 1993, once called probably the best vegetarian restaurant in Britain; give the menu a minute. Monday and Tuesday are dinner from 17:00, other days lunch and dinner with an afternoon gap, to 20:30 most nights.

places.name: Food for Friends
places.note: Vegetarian and vegan since 1981, with brunch every day to noon before the lunch and dinner menus; the easy answer for a group with mixed diets. Open to 22:00 on Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Riddle & Finns
places.note: Oyster and champagne bar with fish and fruits de mer platters; this branch is mostly walk-in with a few daily bookings, so arrive early or join the waitlist. A second branch is on the seafront at 65 Kings Road. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Bincho Yakitori
places.note: A proper izakaya: charcoal-grilled skewers and Japanese small plates rather than sushi-bar standards. Book online if you can, though walk-ins are taken; hours vary, check.

places.name: Volk's Electric Railway
places.note: The world's oldest electric railway still running, since 1883, a mile of seafront from the Aquarium to Black Rock. Seasonal and weather-dependent, effectively shut in winter, so a spring-to-autumn add-on; check the running days.

places.name: Brighton Museum & Art Gallery
places.note: In the Pavilion Gardens, so pair it with the palace: Egyptology through to 20th-century design and fashion, with a Biba show from October 2026 to March 2027. Hours vary, check.

places.name: West Pier
places.note: The iron skeleton of the 1866 pier, all that is left after storm collapses in 2002 and fires in 2003. Free to look at from the beach or the i360's base, not to walk on; best at low tide or sunset.

places.name: The Colonnade Bar
places.note: A Victorian theatre bar in velvet and gilt, walls covered in signed cast photos, open to anyone with or without a show. Fills fast round curtain times at the Theatre Royal next door; open to midnight Friday and Saturday.

places.name: SEA LIFE Brighton
places.note: The world's oldest operating aquarium (1872), Victorian ironwork overhead and a shark and ray tank below; from £16 online, last entry an hour before close. The weekly schedule was not confirmed, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Devil's Dyke
places.note: A 100m-deep V-shaped valley on the South Downs with an Iron Age hillfort and views back to the sea; National Trust land, free, no gates. No rail: a car or the seasonal Breeze Up to the Downs bus from the station.

places.name: Preston Park
places.note: 63 acres of lawns and rose gardens with the world's oldest working velodrome (1877), 10 minutes by train or bus from the seafront. It hosts Pride and the Brighton Marathon finish, so avoid those dates if you want it quiet.

places.name: Windsor Castle
places.note: The oldest and largest occupied castle in the world and still a royal residence, so it can shut at short notice for state events, and St George's Chapel is kept for worship on Sundays. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Bourton-on-the-Water
places.note: The River Windrush runs shallow through the middle of the village under a string of low stone footbridges. There is no station: come by car or a tour coach from Oxford, Bath or Moreton-in-Marsh.

places.name: Bibury
places.note: Arlington Row, a terrace of 17th-century weavers' cottages, is the most photographed street in the Cotswolds; William Morris reportedly called Bibury the most beautiful village in England. No rail: drive or take a tour coach.

places.name: Westminster Abbey
places.note: Henry III's Gothic church, begun 1245, where 40 monarchs have been crowned since 1066, Charles III in 2023. Find Edward the Confessor, Elizabeth I, Newton, Darwin and the Unknown Warrior. £32, book online, 90 minutes; Monday to Saturday, go at 09:30, and it can shut at short notice.

places.name: The National Gallery
places.note: Free, founded 1824: Van Gogh's Sunflowers, Constable's Hay Wain, the Arnolfini Portrait and the Rokeby Venus. Allow 2 hours; daily 10:00 to 18:00 and to 21:00 on Friday, the quiet slot. The free timed ticket is optional, exhibitions cost extra.

places.name: V&A South Kensington
places.note: Free, about 2.8 million objects of art and design. Do the Cast Courts, with a full-size Trajan's Column and David, and the Ardabil Carpet; Fashion is shut until 2028, South Asia until spring 2028. Allow 2.5 hours; daily 10:00 to 17:45, Friday to 22:00.

places.name: Churchill War Rooms
places.note: The basement Churchill's war cabinet ran from 1939 to 1945: the Cabinet Room, the Map Room, the transatlantic telephone room and his bedroom, plus the Churchill Museum. £34, timed tickets online with an audio guide; 2 hours, daily, last entry 17:00, so go first thing.

places.name: Sir John Soane's Museum
places.note: Free: the architect's own house, kept as he left it in 1837 by Act of Parliament. See Seti I's sarcophagus and Hogarth's Rake's Progress in the Picture Room with its hinged walls. Walk-in, expect a queue; 75 minutes, Wednesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:00, last in 16:30.

places.name: St Bartholomew's Church
places.note: Edmund Scott's red-brick church of 1874, 144 ft high and one of the tallest parish churches in England. Look for the 45 ft marble baldacchino and Henry Wilson's Lady altar. No charge is listed; 30 minutes, weekdays 10:00 to 13:00, Saturday to 16:00, Sunday mass 10:30, check.

places.name: Preston Manor & Gardens
places.note: A Georgian house of 1738 over a 13th-century cellar, reopened in 2025 with Edwardian upstairs-downstairs rooms, the servants' basement and a pet cemetery in the walled garden. Friday to Monday 10:00 to 17:00, last in 16:15, season ends 30 November; check the price.

places.name: Booth Museum of Natural History
places.note: Free: Edward Booth's 1874 museum of Victorian bird dioramas, plus drawers of insects, fossils and minerals. Tuesday and Wednesday 12:00 to 17:00, weekends from 10:00, shut Monday, Thursday and Friday; 75 minutes, no booking, go in the afternoon.

places.name: Brighton Toy and Model Museum
places.note: Over 10,000 toys and models under the station approach, open since 1991. £10, no booking needed; 75 minutes. Tuesday to Friday 10:00 to 17:00, Saturday from 11:00, last in 16:30, shut Sunday and Monday.
places.neighborhood: Trafalgar Street, under the station approach

places.name: Hove Museum of Creativity
places.note: Free, in an 1877 Italianate villa: the Wizard's Attic toy gallery, early cinema kit from the 1890s and the Mechanical Circus. An hour; 10:00 to 17:00, shut Tuesday and Wednesday and 22 December to 1 January.

sources: sights-v2 2026-10-28: London and Brighton beds brought to the sights standard; Bath and Oxford already met it

destination.name: South of England: London, Bath, Oxford and Brighton
destination.pitch: Four beds a train ride apart: London for the free museums, markets and the East End, Bath for the Roman spring and Georgian streets, Oxford for colleges and old pubs, Brighton for the seafront. Plan round Mondays and booked slots.
destination.caveat: London is dear and runs on queues and booked slots: the Tower, Sky Garden, the Roman Baths. The Tube mostly stops about 00:30. Bath's centre clogs round the Baths, Oxford colleges close to visitors for exams from late April to June, and Brighton's beach is pebble and windy. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Borough Market to Bankside to the City on foot, Columbia Road on a Sunday, the Royal Crescent and the Circus in Bath, Radcliffe Square in Oxford and the Lanes in Brighton.
because.food: A salt beef beigel on Brick Lane at any hour, pici cacio e pepe at Padella, bone marrow at St. JOHN, scallops at the Chequers in Bath, tapas at Arbequina and surf and turf at the Chilli Pickle.
because.culture: The British Museum, Tate Modern and the Ashmolean all free, a Yeoman Warder tour of the Tower, the Roman Baths, the Holburne, the Pitt Rivers and George IV's Royal Pavilion.
because.exploration: The Grapes in Limehouse, the Turf down its two passages, the 6-mile Bath Skyline loop, the American Museum above the Avon, and Devil's Dyke on the South Downs.
